title: Record every payment as a ledger of provider events
description: A payment is now a record in the back office from the moment the buyer presses a payment button: what is being paid for, by whom, for how much, and every event the provider reported about it. Invoices, events, the shop and the marketplace all pay through it, and the outcome is shown on one result page at `/{workspace}/payments/{reference}` that survives a refresh, a closed tab and a forwarded link. The browser return and the provider's webhook settle through the same ledger, so a payment confirmed after the tab was closed is still recorded and a notification that arrives twice is counted once. A captured payment is booked in the ERP from its own record, with sale order, invoice and invoice payment built together, and a booking that cannot run waits under Portal › Payments › Needs attention with the reason and a retry. A payment left open is followed up with its provider and, when the provider cannot say, listed as having no answer for finance to check. Paying an invoice withdraws the open bank transfers it no longer needs, and a transfer the payer has already funded in part must be completed before the invoice is paid another way. Refunds and disputes are listed for finance to book in the ERP by hand, one entry each, and a dispute decided in the merchant's favour no longer reads charged back. From the ERP, a person can record a capture, cancellation or refund seen in the provider's back office, match an unmatched provider event, retry any payment job, deliver by hand a purchase whose delivery failed, and close a stuck booking with the records booked by hand. A tenant whose database lacks the payment tables has payments turned off, loudly, at startup, and the log names every hour the providers whose webhook is not confirming captures. Upgrading needs the per-tenant steps in the runbook at https://github.com/axelor/goovee/blob/main/migrations/payments.md.
